devices.label: Raspberry Pi 5 SBC
devices.description: BCM2712 quad-core Cortex-A76 SBC with a single gigabit Ethernet port fed by the RP1 I/O controller, plus dual-band 2x2 802.11ac Wi-Fi and Bluetooth 5.0.
devices.notes: 1x 1GbE only - no 2.5GbE on the Pi 5 despite many RK3588 competitors having it. USB ports are not modelled. Existing catalogue entry 'RaspberryPi5' declares eth0 only and omits the onboard radio.

devices.label: Raspberry Pi 4 Model B SBC
devices.description: BCM2711 quad-core Cortex-A72 SBC with one true gigabit Ethernet port (PCIe-attached, not USB-bridged) and dual-band 2x2 802.11ac Wi-Fi with Bluetooth 5.0.
devices.notes: Wireless/BT are absent on the cheaper SKUs sold as 'Pi 4 Model B (no wireless)'; this spec models the standard board. Single RJ45, so router duties are limited to VLAN trunking.

devices.label: Raspberry Pi Compute Module 4
devices.description: SO-DIMM-format BCM2711 module whose gigabit MAC/PHY and optional dual-band 802.11ac radio are only usable through a carrier board that exposes the RJ45 and antenna connectors.
devices.notes: No connectors on the module itself: eth0 assumes a carrier board with an RJ45 (most do), wlan0 assumes a wireless SKU (CM4 has 'Lite' and non-wireless variants). Nice for modelling custom multi-NIC carrier boards.

devices.label: Orange Pi 5 Plus SBC
devices.description: Rockchip RK3588 SBC with two independent 2.5GbE ports (RTL8125 on PCIe) plus an M.2 E-key slot for an optional Wi-Fi 6 module - no radio is fitted on the board.
devices.notes: Dual 2.5G: the cheapest way to get two 2.5G ports in a lab router/firewall role (VyOS/OpenWrt). No onboard Wi-Fi - add a 2230 Wi-Fi 6 module to the M.2 E-key slot and add wlan0 to the model if the lab needs it.

devices.label: Radxa ROCK 5B SBC
devices.description: Rockchip RK3588 SBC with a single 2.5GbE port (PoE with an add-on HAT) and an M.2 E-key slot for a Wi-Fi module; the base 5B ships without a radio.
devices.notes: Single 2.5GbE, no onboard Wi-Fi/BT on the plain 5B (the ROCK 5B+ adds an RTL8852BE Wi-Fi 6 module - model that variant separately if needed). Same RK3588 class as the Orange Pi 5 Plus but half the NICs.

devices.label: Banana Pi BPI-R3 router board
devices.description: OpenWrt-oriented MediaTek MT7986 (Filogic 830) router board: 5x gigabit RJ45 plus 2x 2.5GbE SFP cages, with 4x4 Wi-Fi 6 radios on both 2.4 GHz and 5 GHz.
devices.notes: Port map: eth0 = WAN gigabit RJ45, eth1-eth4 = 4x LAN gigabit RJ45, sfp0/sfp1 = the two 2.5Gbase-X SFP cages (serdes is fixed at 2.5G, so 1G SFPs do not link). Two radios, one interface each: wlan0 = 4x4 2.4 GHz (MT7975N), wlan1 = 4x4 5 GHz (MT7975P). SFP cages are modelled as ethernet with speed 2.5G; SFF modules themselves belong in the optics catalogue.

devices.label: Intel NUC 13 Pro mini PC
devices.description: 4x4-inch 13th-gen Core mini PC with a single Intel i226-V 2.5GbE port plus Intel AX211 Wi-Fi 6E and Bluetooth 5.3.
devices.notes: One 2.5G RJ45 only; the second Thunderbolt 4 port can carry a 10G/2.5G Thunderbolt NIC but that adapter is not modelled. Kit model NUC13ANHi7 already exists in the catalogue with wlan0 at 1G - AX211 is a 2x2 160 MHz Wi-Fi 6E part, so 2.5G is the more accurate radio figure.

devices.label: Beelink SER6 mini PC
devices.description: Ryzen 9 6900HX mini PC with one 2.5GbE RJ45 port and a Wi-Fi 6 (2x2, 2.4 Gbps) radio; the chassis also carries USB4, which is not a NIC.
devices.notes: Single 2.5G port - fine as a virtualisation host or single-legged router, not as a wired multi-port firewall. Several listings advertise '2.5G LAN ports' plural; the SER6 chassis has one RJ45.

devices.label: Minisforum Venus UM790 Pro mini PC
devices.description: Ryzen 9 7940HS mini PC with a single 2.5GbE RJ45 port, Wi-Fi 6E (2x2 160 MHz) and Bluetooth 5.3, plus two USB4 ports.
devices.notes: One 2.5G RJ45, no second wired NIC. USB4/Thunderbolt adapters ignored per the no-USB-NIC rule.

devices.label: Protectli Vault Pro VP2420
devices.description: Fanless Intel Celeron J6412 appliance with four Intel 2.5GbE RJ45 ports (i225-V or i226-V depending on build date) and no wireless; the classic quad-2.5G pfSense/OPNsense box.
devices.notes: 4x 2.5G, no fans, no Wi-Fi - great WAN/LAN/DMZ/OPT lab corner. Existing catalogue copy of VP2420 is categorised 'firewall'; this batch uses 'host' for all SBC/mini-PC/fanless-appliance entries.

devices.label: Protectli Vault Pro VP4670 (6-port 2.5G)
devices.description: Fanless six-port Vault Pro built on an Intel i7-10810U with six Intel i226-V 2.5GbE RJ45 ports and no wireless; the highest-port-count 2.5G Vault Pro.
devices.notes: 6x 2.5G, i7-10810U, M.2 NVMe + 2.5in SATA, 16GB eMMC, micro-USB console. The VP4600 family are 6-port 2.5G boxes (VP4630/VP4630e/VP4650/VP4670); only CPU differs, so this spec covers the family at the top SKU.

devices.label: Qotom Q555G6 6-LAN mini PC
devices.description: Fanless 6-LAN industrial mini PC on an Intel i5-7200U (Skylake-U) with six Intel I210/I211 gigabit RJ45 ports and no wireless.
devices.notes: 6x 1G (not 2.5G): Qotom's 2.5G six-port boxes are separate SKUs (e.g. i225-V 4305U models). Also sold in 1U rack ears - modelled as a host/mini-PC since the board is the desktop unit. Sibling Q750G5 (5x 2.5G) is already in the catalogue.

devices.label: ZimaBoard 832 single-board server
devices.description: Credit-card-sized x86 single-board server with Intel Celeron N3450, two gigabit Ethernet ports and no wireless, plus a PCIe x4 slot for an add-in NIC.
devices.notes: Dual 1G (both gigabit, not 2.5G) and no Wi-Fi at all. The exposed PCIe x4 slot is usually populated with a 2.5G card in router builds - add eth2 at 2.5G in the lab if that card is modelled; the slot itself is not a port.
